failures.title: Vauxhall B15DTE Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: EGR Cooler Leaks - 60k-120k miles
items.whatHappens: The exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) cooler is prone to internal cracking, allowing coolant to leak into the exhaust. This leads to coolant loss, white smoke from the exhaust, and eventually engine overheating. The issue is well-documented across the PSA DV5 family, which shares the same EGR cooler design .
items.repairVsReplace: EGR cooler replacement is typically a £500-£900 repair and is effective if caught early. If the engine has overheated, cylinder head warping may write off the unit - in which case full engine replacement is the only safe option. See our EGR valve failure guide for more detail.

items.title: DPF Clogging - Urban-use pattern
items.onset: Variable - strongly dependent on driving style
items.whatHappens: Like most modern diesels, the B15DTE's diesel particulate filter clogs when the vehicle is used predominantly for short urban trips that prevent regeneration cycles from completing. Symptoms include reduced power, increased fuel consumption, and the DPF warning light .
items.repairVsReplace: A forced regeneration at a specialist costs £150-£300. Replacement DPF units are £400-£1,200. Unlike some other PSA engines, the B15DTE's DPF is not integrated with the catalytic converter on most applications, making replacement cheaper . Read our DPF failure guide for full detail.

items.title: Injector Wear - 80k-120k miles
items.whatHappens: Piezo injectors on the B15DTE can develop leak-off issues, causing rough idle, poor cold starting, increased fuel consumption, and potential diesel contamination of the engine oil. The issue is more common on high-mileage urban-use vehicles .
items.repairVsReplace: Injector refurbishment or replacement is typically £300-£800 per injector. If diesel contamination of the oil has occurred, oil and filter change is essential; neglect leads to bearing damage and engine failure.

failures.goodYearsLine: The B15DTE's EGR cooler design was revised on later production units (approximately post-2021). Vehicles manufactured after this date appear to have fewer reported EGR failures .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the B15DTE
variants.intro: ═══════════════════════════════════════ The B15DTE appears as the 1.5-litre diesel option on Vauxhall Corsa F and Grandland A. It is part of the PSA DV5 family (alongside DV5RC, DV5R, etc.) - a modern common-rail turbodiesel. Where to find your engine code: - On the engine block - stamped on the front face of the cylinder block, visible from the top of the engine bay - On the V5C registration document - check the "Engine number" field - the code will appear as B15DTE followed by a serial number - Via VIN decoder - enter your 17-character VIN into a Vauxhall/Opel VIN decoder online Common confusion: The B15DTE is often confused with: - DV5RC - the same 1.5 diesel in Peugeot/Citroën applications, with different engine mountings and ECU calibration; not interchangeable - B16DTH - Vauxhall's 1.6 CDTi diesel; different displacement, entirely different engine family; not a substitute - A17DTR - the 1.7 CDTi it replaced; different engine mounts, ECU and wiring loom; not a straight swap Why it matters: Fitting the wrong engine code can cause serious issues: - The B15DTE has different electrical connectors, ECU programming, and immobiliser integration than earlier 1.7/1.6 CDTi units - Engine mounts and sump differ between Corsa and Grandland applications Enter your registration above - we'll confirm which sub-code you need and match you to specialists who supply the correct unit.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement B15DTE - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used B15DTE makes sense for lower-value Corsa F (sub-£8k examples) where a reconditioned unit could approach 40-50% of vehicle value. The critical risk is EGR cooler and DPF condition - these are expensive to replace separately, so any used unit must come with evidence of recent work or a strong warranty. Link once: used engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: The proper reconditioned B15DTE addresses the EGR cooler (replaced or ultrasonically cleaned), DPF inspected, and injectors tested. For Corsa and Grandland owners, reconditioned is the sweet spot - the engine is modern enough to justify investment, and the £1,500-£2,800 supply price is significantly cheaper than main dealer new. Link once: reconditioned engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified when the engine has suffered catastrophic failure (e.g., overheated from EGR cooler leak causing head gasket failure) and the vehicle value warrants it. For Grandland owners with vehicles worth £12k-£18k, a rebuild with upgraded EGR cooler and DPF is a viable long-term ownership proposition. Link once: rebuilt engines

items.question: What is the most common failure on the B15DTE engine?
items.answer: The most common B15DTE failure is EGR cooler leaks, which typically appear at 60k-120k miles. Coolant leaks from the EGR cooler cause coolant loss, white exhaust smoke, and eventual overheating if ignored. DPF clogging from urban driving and injector wear (80k-120k miles) are also well-documented patterns across the PSA DV5 family . → Read our full EGR failure guide

items.question: What's the difference between B15DTE and DV5RC (Peugeot 1.5 BlueHDi)?
items.answer: The B15DTE and DV5RC are the same engine family (PSA DW/DV5) fitted to different brands. They are mechanically near-identical but have different ECU calibration and engine mounts for Vauxhall versus Peugeot/Citroën engine bays. The B15DTE is tuned for Vauxhall-specific emissions requirements and uses Vauxhall's electrical architecture and immobiliser system. → Get the correct engine for your vehicle
bullets: DV5RC: Peugeot/Citroën calibration, different engine mount pattern
B15DTE: Vauxhall calibration, different ECU software
They are not interchangeable without significant modification

items.question: How long does a B15DTE engine typically last?
items.answer: A B15DTE diesel engine typically lasts 120,000-180,000 miles with proper maintenance, with many reaching 150k+ before major work is needed. The main longevity threats are EGR cooler failure (which can cause overheating) and DPF clogging (which can lead to engine oil dilution and turbo wear). Regular servicing - especially using PSA-spec low-SAPS oil - is essential for achieving maximum lifespan . → Browse reconditioned B15DTE engines with warranty ═══════════════════════════════════════
bullets: EGR cooler failure (60k-120k) can write off the engine if ignored
DPF clogging is the biggest urban-use threat
Regular oil changes (every 10k miles or annually) are critical
